question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total freight carried by Canadian railways in July 2026, in tonnes, as it will be first reported by Statistics Canada in its monthly Railway carloadings release (total traffic carried, Canada).

target.what: Total freight carried by Canadian railways (all traffic carried, Canada) as first reported by Statistics Canada in the monthly Railway carloadings release for the reference month July 2026; this is the total tonnage carried (carloadings traffic), not revenue ton-km or revenue.
target.caveats: Working interpretation: the headline 'total traffic carried' tonnage for the month, Canada, all commodities and all railway operators covered by the survey (freight only, excluding passenger and non-freight service). Alternatives that would change the answer: (a) total freight vs. domestic-origin-on

candidates.perspective: Statistics Canada Railway carloadings time series
candidates.hypothesis: July total tonnage follows a stable seasonal pattern relative to adjacent months and prior Julys; the target equals the most recent published monthly total scaled by the historical July-to-recent-month ratio and year-over-year trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total traffic carried (tonnes), Canada, all commodities, for July 2023, July 2024, July 2025 and the most recent months published before 2026-08-29 (e.g., May/June 2026 if available); also the July seasonal factor or month-over-month ratio in recent years.
search_hints: Statistics Canada Railway carloadings monthly total traffic carried tonnes
Table 23-10-0219-01 railway carloadings total tonnes July
railway carloadings July 2025 Canada total tonnage

candidates.hypothesis: Total tonnage equals the sum over commodity groups (grain, coal, potash, forest products, chemicals, intermodal, etc.); summing the largest commodity groups' July 2026 tonnages plus a residual share reproduces the headline total.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly tonnage by commodity group for Canada for July 2025 and recent 2026 months, plus the share of total accounted for by the top commodity groups; minimum evidence is the top 5-8 commodity tonnages and their combined share of the total.
search_hints: Statistics Canada railway carloadings by commodity tonnes table
railway carloadings grain coal potash tonnes Canada monthly

candidates.perspective: Grain, potash and coal supply chains
candidates.hypothesis: Bulk commodities dominate tonnage; July tonnage is constrained by western grain movement, potash mine shipments and coal exports, so summing these physical flows (with rail share) plus other commodities approximates the total.
candidates.data_to_find: July 2026 (or latest available) western Canadian grain rail shipments (tonnes), potash rail shipments/exports, and coal rail shipments; rail modal share for each; minimum evidence is at least two of these commodity flows for July 2026 or a close proxy month.

candidates.perspective: Railway operators (CN, CPKC) and carload capacity
candidates.hypothesis: Total tonnage equals loaded car count times average tonnes per car; operator carload volumes and average payload give an independent check on the headline total.
candidates.data_to_find: CN and CPKC July 2026 (or latest) carloadings/volume metrics, average tonnes per carload or per car, and their combined share of Canadian rail tonnage; minimum evidence is one operator's monthly carloads and average payload.
search_hints: average tonnes per railcar Canada grain

candidates.perspective: US Surface Transportation Board / AAR rail traffic
candidates.hypothesis: North American rail traffic moves with similar macro drivers; US rail carload tonnage trends in July 2026 can indicate the direction and magnitude of Canadian July tonnage relative to prior-year Julys.
candidates.data_to_find: US rail carloads/tonnage for July 2026 and July 2025 (AAR or STB), and the historical correlation or ratio between Canadian and US monthly rail tonnage; minimum evidence is the July 2026 US year-over-year change.
search_hints: US rail tonnage July 2026 year over year

candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 tonnage may deviate from seasonal norms due to strikes, wildfires, port disruptions, tariffs or trade policy; measurable exposure (days lost, affected corridors) adjusts the baseline estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Any rail labour action, wildfire/derailment closures, port or border disruptions, or tariff changes affecting Canadian rail freight in July 2026, with dates and estimated tonnage impact; minimum evidence is confirmation of whether a major disruption occurred.

candidates.hypothesis: Published freight or trade forecasts for 2026 and commodity export outlooks constrain the plausible range of July 2026 tonnage relative to 2025.
candidates.data_to_find: 2026 Canadian rail freight or bulk commodity export forecasts, grain/potash/coal production and export guidance for 2026, and any StatCan or industry commentary on 2026 rail volumes; minimum evidence is a 2026 growth expectation for a major commodity.

candidates.hypothesis: If only car counts or ton-km are available, total tonnage can be recovered using average tonnes per car or tonnes per revenue ton-km; the coverage ratio between the survey universe and total Canadian rail traffic is needed.
candidates.data_to_find: Average tonnes per loaded car by commodity, revenue ton-km to tonnage conversion, and the share of Canadian rail traffic captured by the Statistics Canada carloadings survey; minimum evidence is one reliable conversion factor.

assumptions.name: July-to-May seasonal ratio for total traffic
assumptions.rationale: July typically runs near or slightly above spring months as grain and potash move; May 2020 was a COVID-depressed month, so July is expected modestly higher. Range reflects seasonal variability.
assumptions.applies_when: Using May 2020 total as base for a July estimate.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that July tonnage is systematically below May in recent years.

assumptions.name: 2026 level factor vs 2020 total traffic
assumptions.rationale: Canadian rail tonnage has trended modestly upward from the 2020 COVID trough; a small cumulative growth factor over six years is plausible, with wide uncertainty.
assumptions.falsified_by: Recent data showing 2026 tonnage below 2020 levels.

assumptions.name: Average tonnes per loaded car
assumptions.rationale: Payload ceiling 75-85 t but many cars (containers, light loads) far below; 62% of movements under 70 t, so average near 65-70 t.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of average payload outside 55-80 t.

assumptions.name: Loaded cars per month (all traffic)
assumptions.rationale: Rough scale: ~25-28 Mt/month at ~68 t/car implies ~370-410k loaded cars; range covers seasonal and disruption variation.
assumptions.falsified_by: Reported carload counts far outside this range.

assessment.note: Same CEIC/StatCan non-intermodal monthly total series; p1 and p47 are duplicate copies of May 2020, p18/p48 duplicate April 2020. They establish the 2020 level (~24.4 Mt/month non-intermodal) but are a single underlying source, not independent confirmation.
Intermodal series: p5/p43 duplicate May 2020 (3.04 Mt), p44 April 2020, p46 long-run average. Same source; establishes intermodal is roughly 11-12% of total tonnage.

Non-intermodal high (Oct 2018, 28.26 Mt), low (Jul 2009, 16.82 Mt) and 1999-2020 average (21.49 Mt) all describe the same series and bracket a plausible July level; they are bounds/context, not separate measurements.
Cement: May 2020 level and July 2019 all-time high; a small commodity (~0.25-0.36 Mt) that shows July can exceed May for construction-linked commodities, supporting a July/May ratio above 1.

All from one CTRF analysis of 2000-2009 carload data: weight limits 75-85 t, many light/volume-constrained cars, container 14.7% of tonnage. Consistent internally but a single source and a stale decade; usable only as a payload/tonnage-mix prior, not as a 2026 measurement.

assumptions.name: July-to-May seasonal ratio for total traffic
assumptions.rationale: July is peak grain/potash/construction season; cement July 2019 high (p12) exceeds May 2020 (p11), and the 1999-2020 mean (p4) sits between the July 2009 low and October 2018 high, implying July is typically near or slightly above the annual mean. May 2020 was COVID-depressed, so July/May should be modestly above 1.
assumptions.applies_when: The May 2020 base is representative of a normal May after adjusting for the 2026 level factor.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that July tonnage is systematically below May in recent years, or that May 2020 was not depressed relative to July.

assumptions.name: 2026 level factor vs 2020 total traffic
assumptions.rationale: Canadian rail tonnage grew from the 2020 COVID trough; the 1999-2020 mean (p4) and 2018 high (p2) bracket a recovery. A modest factor above 1 reflects post-2020 recovery plus grain/potash growth, tempered by tariff and wildfire risk in 2026.
assumptions.applies_when: 2026 traffic is broadly comparable in scope to the 2020 CEIC series (all traffic, Canada).
assumptions.falsified_by: Published 2024-2026 totals showing tonnage flat or below 2020 levels.

assumptions.name: Average tonnes per loaded car
assumptions.rationale: CTRF weight limits are 75-85 t (p31, p32) but 62% of movements are under 70 t (p34) and 60% are volume-constrained (p36); a tonnage-weighted average near 68 t is consistent with bulk hoppers/gondolas dominating tonnage (p40, p41) while light cars dominate counts.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to loaded car counts for all traffic.
assumptions.falsified_by: Operator data showing average payload materially outside 55-80 t.

assumptions.name: Loaded cars per month (all traffic)

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
